arxiv-2104-12485.title: Powered Dirichlet Process for Controlling the Importance of “Rich-Get-Richer” Prior Assumptions in Bayesian Clustering
arxiv-2104-12485.creator: Gael Poux-Medard, Julien Velcin, Sabine Loudcher
arxiv-2104-12485.description: Abstract One of the most used priors in Bayesian clustering is the Dirichlet prior. It can be expressed as a Chinese Restaurant Process. This process allows nonparametric estimation of the number of clusters when partitioning datasets. Its key feature is the “rich-get-richer” property, which assumes a cluster has an a priori probability to get chosen linearly dependent on population.

arxiv-2204-01899.title: MonoTrack: Shuttle trajectory reconstruction from monocular badminton video
arxiv-2204-01899.creator: Paul Liu, Jui-Hsien Wang
arxiv-2204-01899.description: Abstract Trajectory estimation is a fundamental component of racket sport analytics, as the trajectory contains information not only about the winning and losing of each point, but also how it was won or lost. In sports such as badminton, players benefit from knowing the full 3D trajectory, as the height of shuttlecock or ball provides valuable tactical information.

arxiv-2310-02993.title: Finding coherent node groups in directed graphs
arxiv-2310-02993.creator: Iiro Kumpulainen, Nikolaj Tatti
arxiv-2310-02993.description: Abstract Summarizing a large graph by grouping the nodes into clusters is a standard technique for studying the given network. Traditionally, the order of the discovered groups does not matter. However, there are applications where, for example, given a directed graph, we would like to find coherent groups while minimizing the backward cross edges.

arxiv-2404-14482.title: Boosting Beyond: A Novel Approach to Probing Top-Philic Resonances at the LHC
arxiv-2404-14482.creator: Luc Darmé, Benjamin Fuks, Hao-Lin Li, Matteo Maltoni, Olivier Mattelaer, Julien Touchèque
arxiv-2404-14482.description: Abstract We introduce a novel search strategy for heavy top-philic resonances that induce new contributions to four-top production at the LHC. We capitalize on recent advances in top-tagging performance to demonstrate that the final state, that is expected to be boosted based on current limits, can be fully reconstructed and exploited.

arxiv-2406-17038.title: modeLing : A Novel Dataset for Testing Linguistic Reasoning in Language Models
arxiv-2406-17038.creator: Nathan A. Chi, Teodor Malchev, Riley Kong, Ryan A. Chi, Lucas Huang, Ethan A. Chi, R. Thomas McCoy, Dragomir Radev
arxiv-2406-17038.description: Abstract We introduce modeLing 1 1 1 Dataset available at https://github.com/nathanchi/modeLing . , a novel benchmark of Linguistics Olympiad-style puzzles which tests few-shot reasoning in AI systems. Solving these puzzles necessitates inferring aspects of a language’s grammatical structure from a small number of examples.

arxiv-2408-02805.title: Numerical Instability of Algebraic Rootfinding Methods Thanks:
arxiv-2408-02805.creator: Emil Graf and Alex Townsend
arxiv-2408-02805.description:
A 2024 arXiv research paper by Emil Graf and Alex Townsend. We demonstrate that the most popular variants of all common algebraic multidimensional rootfinding algorithms are unstable by analyzing the conditioning of subproblems that are constructed at intermediate steps. In particular, we give multidimensional polynomial systems for which the conditioning of a subproblem can be worse than the conditioning of the original problem by a factor that grows exponentially with the number of variables. keywords

polynomial systems, numerical instability, rootfinding

Funding. was supported by NSF GRFP (DGE-2139899).

arxiv-2508-02251.title: Orientational Effects in the Low Pair Continuum of Aluminium Publication type: ORIGINAL ARTICLE
arxiv-2508-02251.creator: Thomas Gawne*, Zhandos A. Moldabekov †, Oliver S. Humphries, Motoaki Nakatsutsumi, Sebastian Schwalbe, Jan Vorberger, Ulf Zastrau, Tobias Dornheim, Thomas R. Preston §
arxiv-2508-02251.description: Abstract We compare the predictions of the dynamic structure factor (DSF) of ambient polycrystalline aluminium from time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) in the pair continuum regime to recent ultrahigh resolution x-ray Thomson scattering measurements, collected at the European XFEL. TDDFT predicts strong anisotropy in the DSF at the wavenumber examined here, even with q q -blurring accounted for.

arxiv-2512-07279.title: Verifiable Deep Quantitative Group Testing
arxiv-2512-07279.creator: Shreyas Jayant Grampurohit shreyasgrampurohit@gmail.com, Satish Mulleti mulleti.satish@gmail.com, Ajit Rajwade ajitvr@cse.iitb.ac.in
arxiv-2512-07279.description: Abstract We present a neural network-based framework for solving the quantitative group testing (QGT) problem that achieves both high decoding accuracy and structural verifiability. In QGT, the objective is to identify a small subset of defective items among N N candidates using only M ≪ N M\ll N pooled tests, each reporting the number of defectives in the tested subset.

arxiv-2512-23552.title: Beyond Per-Thread Lock Sets: Multi-Thread Critical Sections and Dynamic Deadlock Prediction
arxiv-2512-23552.creator: Martin Sulzmann
arxiv-2512-23552.description: Abstract . Lock sets are commonly used for dynamic analysis of deadlocks. The standard per-thread lock set construction only considers locks acquired in the same thread, but is unaware of locks acquired in another thread. This leads to false positives and false negatives.

pmc-11400648.title: A postmortem high-resolution MRI study of the development of cochlear nerve-related structures in the second and third trimesters of pregnancy
pmc-11400648.creator: Hui Zhao, Lixin Sun, Lianxiang Xiao, Linsheng Wang, Na Hu, Mingming Miao, Daniel Thomas Ginat, Carlo A. Mallio, Xiangtao Lin

This study sought to provide imaging data for clinical evaluations concerning cochlear nerve development in the fetus using MRI.MethodsPostmortem 3.

pmc-12374317.title: Determinants of health facility choice for delivery among women participating in group antenatal care in Machakos county, kenya: A cross-sectional survey
pmc-12374317.creator: Jefferson Mwaisaka, Pooja Sripad, Melanie Olum, Patricia Owira, Samuel Mwaura, Rhoda Njeru, Daniel Muli, Faith Mutisya, Anne Hyre, Lisa Noguchi, Stephanie Suhowatsky
pmc-12374317.description: BackgroundGroup antenatal (G-ANC) care has been introduced in Kenya and is associated with increased ANC contacts. Previous studies did not report higher likelihood of facility-based deliveries, where facility delivery rates are high (> 80%). It is unknown whether G-ANC influences women’s choice of delivery facility.

pmc-12492820.title: Barriers to primary health care: perspectives of marginalized Roma women and healthcare professionals
pmc-12492820.creator: Jana Marosnikova Plavnicka, Zuzana Dankulincova Veselska, Daniela Filakovska Bobakova
pmc-12492820.description: BackgroundMarginalized Roma communities (MRCs) in Slovakia experience longstanding exclusion from essential services, including healthcare. Roma women, in particular, face compounded vulnerabilities that contribute to unequal access and poorer health outcomes. Despite increasing attention to these issues, a deeper understanding of the lived experiences that shape healthcare access in MRCs remains necessary.

pmc-12618536.title: Bidirectional quantitative scattering microscopy
pmc-12618536.creator: Kohki Horie, Keiichiro Toda, Takuma Nakamura, Takuro Ideguchi
pmc-12618536.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Quantitative phase microscopy (QPM) and interferometric scattering (iSCAT) microscopy are powerful label-free imaging techniques that are widely used in biomedical applications. Each method, however, possesses distinct limitations: QPM, which measures forward scattering (FS), excels at imaging microscale structures but struggles with rapidly moving nanoscale objects, whereas iSCAT, based on backward scattering (BS), is highly sensitive to nanoscale dynamics but lacks the ability to comprehensively image microscale structures.

pmc-12619540.title: Five-Year Review of Pediatric Vascular Trauma Patterns and Management in Conflict Zones: Insights from Somalia
pmc-12619540.creator: Abdijalil Abdullahi Ali, Fatima Mohamud Ahmed, Abdinafic Mohamud Hussein, Hassan Kalif Abdi II, Ahmed Omar Mohamed Snr, Ali Mohamed Warsame Keilie, Mohamed Omar Hassan, Said Abdirahman Ahmed
pmc-12619540.description: BackgroundPediatric vascular trauma is uncommon but devastating, and risk is amplified in conflict zones with constrained systems. Evidence from Somalia is limited.ObjectiveTo describe patterns, mechanisms, anatomic distribution, management, and outcomes of pediatric vascular trauma over five years at a tertiary referral center in Mogadishu.MethodsRetrospective study of patients ≤18 years with traumatic vascular injury (April 2019–April 2024).

pmc-12649909.title: Ecotone-Driven Vegetation Transitions Reshape Soil Nitrogen Cycling Functional Genes in Black Soils of Northeast China
pmc-12649909.creator: Junnan Ding, Yingjian Wang, Shaopeng Yu
pmc-12649909.description: Simple SummaryUnderstanding how vegetation transitions influence soil microbial processes is essential for predicting nutrient cycling and greenhouse gas dynamics in ecotone ecosystems. In this study, we examined soils along a forest–wetland gradient in Northeast China, where fertile black soils serve as both agricultural and ecological resources.

pmc-13119214.title: Rare-Earth Elements at the Interface of Chemistry and Cancer Therapy
pmc-13119214.creator: Christian Goldiș, Nicoleta Anamaria Pașcalău, Roxana Racoviceanu, Tamara Maksimovic, Mihaela Jorgovan, Elisabeta Atyim, Oana Bătrîna, Marius Mioc, Codruța Șoica
pmc-13119214.description: Rare-earth elements (REEs), which include the entire lanthanide series together with scandium and yttrium, have unique electronic configurations and coordination chemical properties that provide them with special magnetic, optical, and redox abilities. Generally used for diagnostic imaging and theranostic applications, increasing evidence emphasizes their potential as direct anticancer agents.

pmc-13349341.title: A Randomised Feasibility Trial of a Service‐Coordinated Exercise Intervention in First‐Episode Psychosis: Challenges in Implementation and Outcome Assessment
pmc-13349341.creator: Brian W. O'Mahony, Elizabeth Wycherley, Karen Daly, Meghan Cowman, Edgar Lonergan, Abigale Owens, Karen O'Mahony, Brian O'Donoghue, Gerard Clarke, Karen O'Connor
pmc-13349341.description: BackgroundPsychosis is increasingly recognised as a systemic disorder characterised by interrelated metabolic dysfunction, chronic low‐grade inflammation and sedentary lifestyles. Physical exercise is a promising intervention to address this triad. This pilot study investigated the feasibility and systemic impact of a pragmatic exercise intervention within a first‐episode psychosis (FEP) service.

uslaw-usc-t34-s21701.title: 34 U.S.C. § 21701 — Definitions
uslaw-usc-t34-s21701.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t34-s21701.description: United States Code, Title 34 (Crime Control And Law Enforcement); Chapter 217 (Elder Abuse Prevention And Prosecution). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. In this chapter— (1) the terms “abuse”, “adult protective services”, “elder”, “elder justice”, “exploitation”, “law enforcement”, and “neglect” have the meanings given those terms in section 1397j of title 42; (2) the term “elder abuse” includes abuse, neglect, and exploitation.
